_about: Anti-aircraft battery: the strike's defence (Alex's decision strike-plan, 2026-10-10: two batteries whose flak uses the cone system aimed upward, strong in the low and medium bands and weak in the high one). A STATIC unit (mobility 'static'): it never moves, turns or plans; its one weapon, FLAK, is an all-around cone aimed UP with flexible-gun tracking. Its band is the surface; it goes down with the fate 'destroyed' at 0 health, so bombs can silence it. EVERY NUMBER IS PROPOSED by Track S2 (2026-10-10); the bands come out as Alex asked from two numbers, the cone's lowest angle (2 degrees: nothing is out of the cone for being low) and the effective range (900 m, reach 1,080 m with the common 20 percent overshoot), which sits just under the high band's height (1,000 m). A plane flying straight over ONE battery takes, in expected pips (scripts/test_support/strike_tuning.gd, table A): bomber low 3.4, medium 2.7, high 0.35; light fighter low 2.3, medium 2.2, high 0.3. Two batteries on a bomber's bomb run at the tower (table C): it loses about half its 8 pips by the time the bombs land at low and medium (3.7 and 4.0), 0.2 at high. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Anti-aircraft battery

size_m._reason: a gun pit, a sandbag ring and two or three guns seen from above

actions_per_turn._reason: a static unit has nothing to plan: one step a turn that stands still

health._reason: a bomb's direct hit is 3 pips and a near miss 2 or 1 (data/sim/bombs.json): a battery goes down to two near hits or a direct hit and a graze, so the bomber can silence one on its way in at the price of bombs the tower needs

sight_range_m._reason: spotters with the guns: sees about as far as a fighter's 800 m, a little less; the enemy AI counts what its units see (scripts/sim/ai_sense.gd), including its static units, so this is how far a battery warns the patrol

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: static: never turns (the exponent is unused; it must be a number)

altitude_bands._reason: it stands on the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json)

hardpoints._reason: Track S2: the guns' muzzles about six metres above the ground, at the battery's centre; the height is part of the cone's geometry (a plane at 120 m is 114 m above the muzzle)

mount_deg._reason: Track S2: the cone is all around (half_across 180), so the mount does not matter; 0 is the battery's heading

half_across_deg._reason: Track S2: all around. 180 means the azimuth is not part of the cone test (combat.gd): flak fires at anything above it, whichever way the battery faces

elevation_deg._reason: Track S2: Alex's accepted proposal, flak on upward cones. The cone is centred 46 degrees above the horizon

half_height_deg._reason: Track S2: from 2 degrees above the horizon to straight up (90). 2 and not 10: a first try with a 10 degree floor left the low band (120 m) out of the cone beyond 680 m of ground distance and made it the LEAST dangerous band (measured at a base chance of 0.05: 1.8 pips a pass against the medium band's 1.9); with a 2 degree floor the cone's edge is the weapon's range (892 m at 120 m) and the low band comes out strongest (3.4 pips a pass against the medium band's 2.7)

effective_range_m._reason: Track S2: strong in the low and medium bands, weak in the high one (Alex's accepted proposal). 900 m effective, 1,080 m reach with the common range_overshoot (data/sim/combat.json): the low band is inside the effective range out to 892 m of ground distance, the medium band out to 806 m; a plane overhead in the high band (1,000 m) is in the fringe at 42 percent of the odds, 200 m to one side at 26 percent, 400 m to one side at nothing

base_hit_chance._reason: Track S2: a battery makes 0.14 hits a second on a plane in the cone before the other factors (two rolls a second at 0.07). Tuned in the tuning tables: at 0.05 a bomber lost 2.8 pips of 8 to two batteries before its bombs landed from low and 3.2 from medium and was never shot down from low, which is not 'strong'; at 0.07 it loses 3.7 and 4.0 and is shot down 1 and 11 percent of the time (aligned runs)

rim_odds_factor._reason: Track S2: flat, as the other flexible guns and turrets: a gun crew aims within the arc

falloff_exponent._reason: Track S2: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: Track S2: flexible-gun tracking (Alex's accepted proposal), 20 deg/s like the bomber's nose gun and the heavy fighter's rear gunner. A bomber overhead at 400 m crosses the line of sight at about 12 deg/s (factor 0.73); at 120 m at about 40 deg/s (0.2): flak cannot swing fast enough for a plane right overhead at low height, so the low band is most dangerous on the approach and the way out. Doubling it to 40 changed a pass over a battery by under 10 percent, so it is not the lever

damage_pips._reason: Track S2: a burst is one pip, like a machine gun's hit; a bomber's 8 pips and a light fighter's 3 are weighed against it

rolls_per_second._reason: Track S2: the same burst rate as every machine gun in the game
